Daily extraterrestrial radiation

Source: R/forcing-derived.R
ef_ra_daily.Rd

Computes the daily extraterrestrial radiation \(R_a\), the solar radiation received on a horizontal surface at the top of the atmosphere during one day, from the latitude and the day of year (FAO-56).

Usage

ef_ra_daily(lat, doy)

Arguments

lat

Numeric. Latitude \(\phi\) [rad], in [-pi/2, pi/2], positive north. Degrees must be converted (deg * pi / 180, FAO-56 Eq. 22).

doy

Numeric. Day of year \(J\), whole number in 1-366.

Value

A numeric vector of daily extraterrestrial radiation \(R_a\) [MJ m-2 d-1] with the common length of the inputs, keeping their dim.

Details

$$R_a = \frac{24 \cdot 60}{\pi} G_{sc} d_r \left[\omega_s \sin\phi \sin\delta + \cos\phi \cos\delta \sin\omega_s\right]$$ with \(G_{sc}\) = 0.0820 MJ m-2 min-1 (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 21; the package constant of the solar constant), the inverse relative distance \(d_r\) (Eq. 23), the declination \(\delta\) (Eq. 24) and the sunset hour angle \(\omega_s = \arccos(-\tan\phi \tan\delta)\) (Eq. 25). The declination and \(d_r\) are the internal helpers shared with ef_solar_geometry().

Polar day and night: where \(|\tan\phi \tan\delta| > 1\) the argument of the arc cosine is limited to [-1, 1], which gives the geometric limits \(\omega_s = \pi\) (24 h of sun) and \(\omega_s = 0\) (no sun, \(R_a = 0\)). FAO-56 (Eqs. 26-27) handles the same case with X = 0.00001 and notes that the daily equation has limited validity in winter at latitudes above 55 degrees (north or south).

Missing values propagate. Latitudes outside [-pi/2, pi/2] (for example given in degrees), doy outside 1-366 or infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error; a non-integer doy raises earthflux_input_error.

Verification status

VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eqs. 21-25; cases V7 and V9: 20 degrees S on 3 September gives 32.2 MJ m-2 d-1). The same equations are ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eqs. 21-24 and 27-29 (pp. 23-25), written with \(G_{sc}\) = 4.92 MJ m-2 h-1 and the factor 24 / pi (identical to 0.0820 MJ m-2 min-1 and 24 * 60 / pi). The limitation of the arc cosine argument in polar conditions is an implementation choice (dev/specs/weather-forcing.md 13).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other derived meteorological variables: ef_dewpoint(), ef_ea, ef_es(), ef_es_slope(), ef_psychrometric(), ef_ra_period(), ef_rso(), ef_wind_2m()

Examples

# FAO-56 example 8: 20 degrees S, 3 September (J = 246)
ef_ra_daily(lat = -20 * pi / 180, doy = 246)
#> [1] 32.194

# Annual course in central Chile
ra <- ef_ra_daily(lat = -35 * pi / 180, doy = 1:365)
range(ra)
#> [1] 15.57067 44.42725
